scenarios.title: A creature cast for its blitz cost has haste, is sacrificed at the end step and draws a card when it dies

setup.notes: Riveteers Requisitioner (3/1) has blitz {2}{R}. Barkweave Crusher (2/5) is B's only creature and has been under B's control since earlier turns.

decisions: A casts Riveteers Requisitioner for its blitz cost {2}{R}, tapping three Mountains. Both players pass; it resolves.
A moves to combat and declares Riveteers Requisitioner as an attacker.
Combat damage is dealt. Both players pass priority through the rest of the turn, including the end step.

variants.label: blitz_unblocked
variants.expected: Riveteers Requisitioner is a legal attacker despite entering this turn (haste) and deals 3 combat damage: B is at 17. At the beginning of the end step it is sacrificed and moves to A's graveyard; A draws a card (hand: Mountain, library: 1 card) from the blitz dies-trigger and a Treasure token is created from its own dies-trigger.

variants.label: hard_cast
variants.delta: A casts Riveteers Requisitioner for its mana cost {1}{R}, tapping two Mountains, instead of its blitz cost.
variants.expected: Riveteers Requisitioner has no haste and cannot be declared as an attacker (summoning sick). B stays at 20. It is not sacrificed at the end step, stays on the battlefield and A draws no card.

variants.label: blitz_blocked
variants.delta: B declares Barkweave Crusher as a blocker of Riveteers Requisitioner.
variants.expected: Barkweave Crusher deals 2 damage to the 3/1 Requisitioner, which dies in the combat damage step; A draws a card from the blitz dies-trigger at that moment and a Treasure token is created. Crusher survives with 3 damage. B stays at 20. At the end step there is nothing left to sacrifice.
